rule: The Miri-admitted TCB suite is machine-owned and fail-closed. `forensics/tools/miri_tcb_suite.py --record` parses a real `cargo +nightly miri test --lib miri_tcb` log and fails unless every name in `admitted` ran and passed, no name in `unsupported` ran, and no `miri_tcb` test in the log is absent from both lists. It never treats a missing run as a pass. The `admitted` set is the subset of the crate that Miri can execute because it allocates through a Rust-backed shim instead of libc; the `unsupported` entries name the surface Miri refuses (libc FFI, DSOs, ucontext/intrinsics) with the reason, rather than being silently skipped.

unsupported.reason: reaches the default branch, whose allocator is the libc malloc FFI; Miri refuses a foreign function
the installed shims forward to libc malloc/realloc/free, so calling them is a foreign function
allocates through the default branch (libc malloc) before any shim can be installed
dlopen/dlsym/dlclose are foreign functions; DSO symbol addresses are the explicit provenance TCB
the ucontext fibre path calls the C shim (openssl_rs_ucontext_*) and makecontext/swapcontext
getrandom/getentropy and the syscall surface are foreign functions
the timestamp path uses inline asm / the rdtsc intrinsic, which Miri does not execute
pthread and futex calls are foreign functions; Miri models only its own thread primitives
